summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Bilgic Der Beruf eines Kesselverzinkers/27)

data.turoyo: Bi makina nəqšinawəlle, sayminawo at tarʕaṯṯe, bu šəklawo sayminawo i ṣopa.
data.translation: Wir verzierten sie in der Maschine und wir fertigten ihre Türen, in der Art und Weise stellten wir den Ofen her.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa box; explicit machine instrument and decorated metal patient, without asserting engraving or embossing.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/149)

data.turoyo: Hənnək hē hənnək taʔile, nuqšíwaynanne bu+kalšooo. ʕAwwǝ́li ḥamməš, bəṯr tlaṯ, bəṯr tarte, ŭ bəṯr ḥḏo.
data.translation: While they were still wet, we would paint them with lime. First five (markings), then three, then two, then one.

rationale: Thin new I Infectum-wa cell; wet vessels, lime medium and pattern sequence are explicit.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/151)

data.translation: We would paint them like so, till eight days, ten days ...

rationale: Thin new I Infectum-wa cell; attests hul with a manufacturing-phase limit, whose precise attachment remains an editorial question.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/64)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr g̊saymíwaynanne k̇avik̇at ŭ čəmbəlk̇at, ŭ bəṯr gəmnaqšíwaynale bu+kalšo, ʕawwəli ḥamməš, bəṯr tlaṯ, ŭ bəṯr tarte, ŭ bəṯr ḥḏo.
data.translation: Then we would make for them edges and handles, and then we would adorn it with lime, first five, then three, and then two, and then one.

rationale: New active II Infectum-wa box, contrasting with the existing Detransitive nominal forms.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) bestickt, bemalt, geschminkt sein;
rationale: Explicit label for the inherited unnumbered I result-state use, supported by nqišo/nqiše with ceiling, eyes and gold-decorated clothes; no new semantic split.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) verziert, gemustert sein;
rationale: Explicit label for the inherited unnumbered II result-state use: natural snake pattern, ornamented stone and embellished veils. This does not assert a human decorating agent.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Famine/64)

data.turoyo: Uʕdo kito naqqəš bu+šəklawo, hawxa konəqši.
data.translation: Now there is decoration in that type, they decorate like so.

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell; active I alongside II in the same verse, with naqqəš treated as noun.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (PrS 78/92)

data.translation: Man brachte ihr nun seidene mit Gold durchwirkte Kleider,

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC NE interview 1/5)

data.turoyo: kə́twaylan əmmíwayna bušiyat dabrisam kome, ʕal haqqa mnaqšéwayne čəzgəliyat yaroqe, šaʕuṯe, pamba, ar+rišikaṯṯe haqqa,
data.translation: we had, we would say, black bridal veils of silk, that would be embellished so much with green, yellow, and pink stripes, their fringes so long ...

rationale: II Part. Pass. with plural past copula and garment patient; a different result-state from stone and snake patterns.

summary: Translate naqšat ʕatiqe as old paintings.
rationale: The Turoyo phrase is ban naqšat ʕatiqe, with the adjective ʕatiqe “old”. The second all in the English sentence does not translate that adjective and is an evident slip for old. The supplied batch also illustrates the same adjective in 1/16: u bayto ʕatiqo we, translated war das Haus alt.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
rationale: Machine ornamentation in Bilgic /27 and objectless konəqši in MAC Famine/64 justify general decoration as well as the inherited specific techniques. Engraving/embossing is not established.

summary: Active I and II appear in the same MAC Famine/64 account. II gəmnaqšíwaynale has active Infectum-wa, while I konəqši has Infectum. Assign from form, not from which German/English gloss sounds closest.
Part. Pass. distinguishes I nqišo/nqiše from II mnaqšo/mnaqašto/mnaqše. The inherited I box contains two mnaqš- personal-communication examples; propose moving them without altering their words.
Past copula -wayne in mnaqšéwayne marks a predicated result-state, not an active Infectum-wa verb.
naqqəš after kito in Famine/64 is a noun, as are pattern nouns naqšat; no extra finite tokens are invented.
neqošo is already filed under II Detransitive Infinitiv at 94/15. The purpose-of-tools context denotes decoration, without independently proving a Detransitive event.
No idiom or technique-specific new sense is established by material b-phrases alone.
In Bilgic /27, does machine nqš mean engraving, embossing, painting, or another ornamenting operation?
At 70/108, is konəšqo an edition transposition or dialect metathesis? Confirm nqš rather than nšq without silently correcting the source.
Does MAC Interview 2/151 hul eight/ten days delimit painting, drying, or the whole production phase?
Confirm neqošo's II Detransitive Infinitiv placement versus active I Infinitiv; keep inherited classification pending the paradigm.
Confirm the two proposed I-to-II p.c. participle moves. The church translation 'all paintings' is inherited and is not silently rewritten.
Metal machine decoration and vessel lime-painting expand the material range, without proving a specific engraving technique.
Natural snake markings and manufactured patterns share the ornamented/patterned state; natural patterning does not entail a decorating agent.
